section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Anatomy of a Cone and Plane
section_1.content: Briefly introduce the 'Double Napped Cone' (two cones meeting at a vertex) and a slicing plane. Establish the concept that the angle of the plane relative to the cone's axis determines the shape of the intersection.
section_1.example: Visualizing a laser pointer beam hitting a flat surface at different angles to create circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

section_2.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Define the Dandelin Spheres: spheres placed inside the cone that are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the slicing plane (at a single point). These points are the 'Foci' of the conic section.
section_2.example: Imagine a 'magic marble' trapped inside a funnel, perfectly touching the cone's surface and a glass sheet covering the funnel.

section_3.title: Visual Proof: The Ellipse Case
section_3.content: Explain that the distance from any point on the ellipse to the two focal points (the tangency points of the two spheres) is constant. This bridges the geometric intersection with the algebraic definition of an ellipse.
section_3.example: Using a diagram showing a 'Planet' (point on the ellipse) orbiting two 'Gravity Anchors' (the foci) where the sum of distances remains constant.

section_4.title: Generalization to Parabola and Hyperbola
section_4.content: Explain how changing the plane's slope forces one sphere to move to infinity (parabola) or move to the other nap of the cone (hyperbola). Emphasize that the tangency point logic holds for all three shapes.
section_4.example: An animation showing a satellite (the plane) changing its trajectory around a planet, transitioning from a circular orbit to a parabolic escape path.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap the core takeaway: Dandelin spheres provide the elegant link between 3D spatial geometry (cones) and 2D locus definitions (foci).
section_5.example: A final visual overlay showing the 'Glow' of the tangency points on the plane, highlighting that the Foci are the 'secret DNA' of every conic section.
